articles.title: El entrenador del Girona explota por una vergonzosa agresión a Iyana Martín: "Está de moda pegarle de h..."
articles.standfirst: Roberto Íñiguez, muy crítico con la agresora Radostina Dimitrova y con los árbitros: "Me cago y me meo si no se puede usar el instant replay".
articles.summary: Roberto Íñiguez, muy crítico con la agresora Radostina Dimitrova y con los árbitros: "Me cago y me meo si no se puede usar el instant replay".
articles.body: Iyana Martín sufrió una agresión en el partido de Eurocup que el Spar Girona disputó este jueves ante el BC Montana 2003 búlgaro. Faltaban 6:28 para el final y las catalanas ganaban por un cómodo 81-57 (acabarían venciendo por 96-71) cuando, aprovechando un bloqueo, Radostina Dimitrova le dio un tremendo codazo en la nuca a propósito a la base española, que se quedó tendida en el parqué con muestras de dolor. Martín tuvo que ser atendida sobre la cancha, se fue al banquillo aturdida y ayudada por miembros del cuerpo técnico del Spar Girona. No volvió a pisar la pista y, después del partido, tuvo que estar en observación después del golpe recibido. Roberto Íñiguez, entrenador del Spar Girona, fue muy crítico en rueda de prensa. "No me puedo callar. No me ha parecido correcto lo que ha pasado con Dimitrova. Creo que ha sido adrede y lo peor ha sido su actitud, riéndose y jaleándose como: 'Ya os he dicho que le iba a dar", dijo el técnico. Al parecer, en el reciente partido de las Ventanas FIBA entre España y Bulgaria ya había habido algún pique entre ambas jugadoras y la búlgara, por lo visto, no se olvidó. "Tenemos a una jugadora que a ver qué pasa. Parece que es el muñeco del pim-pam-pum ahora. Está de moda pegarle de hostias a Iyana", se quejó el entrenador vitoriano, que recibió una técnica por protestar pidiendo más castigo para la agresora, que fue sancionada con una falta flagrante: "No ha sido justo lo que han pitado los árbitros. Deberían haber descalificado a esta jugadora. Hay que jugar duro, pero eso no es jugar duro, eso es de ser una sinvergüenza". Íñiguez cuestionó la labor de los colegiados y el uso del instant replay. "Los tres árbitros me dicen que no pueden verlo porque no hay. Bueno, bien, primero sí hay. Luego, no lo puedes usar en Eurocup, cosa que me cago y me meo, que no se puede usar el instant replay. Si tenemos la máquina y tenemos la instalación y la tecnología, ¿por qué no se usa el instant replay? A ver, que alguien me lo explique. Lo ha visto todo el mundo y tres no lo habéis visto. Pues no lo entiendo", lamentó.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Cameron Brink's family connection makes Ayesha's bridesmaid role even more special at Stanford wedding
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha were at Stanford Memorial Church on Nov. 14 when WNBA star Cameron Brink married her longtime partner, Ben Felter.
articles.body: Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha were at Stanford Memorial Church on Nov. 14 when WNBA star Cameron Brink married her longtime partner, Ben Felter. Ayesha stood with the bridesmaids, a role with years of shared history behind it. The Golden State Warriors guard and the Sparks player have known each other since childhood, and their families have been close for just as long. Vogue published photos from the day ten days later. The couple celebrated at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay with family, friends, and Brink's Sparks teammates.Why does the Curry family connection matter at Cameron Brink's wedding?Stephen Curry and Brink are god-siblings. They have known each other since childhood, and the link runs through both families. Their fathers played together at Virginia Tech. Their mothers were college roommates. Curry's mother, Sonya, is Brink's godmother, and she had a part in the ceremony itself. For Curry, being there meant a lot for that reason.One photo in the Vogue feature shows Sonya praying over the newlyweds. Brink wrote the caption herself: "My wonderful godmother Sonya praying over us."Ayesha's spot among the bridesmaids fits that history. The Currys' daughter, Ryan, was the flower girl and later sang "Until I Found You" during the first dance. Curry and Ayesha also posed for a photo with Brink and Felter during the celebration.The groom had kind words for the pair as well. "Hope to build a family as beautiful as Steph and Ayesha's one day," Felter wrote. The groom named their marriage as the example he wants to follow in his own.Stanford ceremony, Half Moon Bay reception and WNBA reactionsThe couple picked Stanford for the ceremony because it is their alma mater, and it is where they met as students in 2020. The reception moved to the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay. Guests got an outdoor cocktail hour, speeches, dancing and a cigar lounge, with floral arrangements and greenery throughout the venue. Curry and Ayesha were among several high-profile guests there. The wedding party wore custom outfits, and the newlyweds rode to the reception in a 1957 Rolls-Royce.The ceremony fell on a Saturday. Ten days later, Brink and Felter shared photos with Vogue and sat down for an interview about how they planned the day. John & Joseph Photography took the pictures. The pictures drew quick reactions from the WNBA. Caitlin Clark liked the Instagram post, and Angel Reese left a "gorgggg" in the comments. Nneka Ogwumike, Skylar Diggins, Paige Bueckers and Lexie Hull wrote congratulations as well, along with Olympian Lindsey Vonn. articles.title: Donovan Mitchell gives Jalen Brunson credit for his achievements with the New York Knicks
articles.summary: Donovan Mitchell and Jalen Brunson have played against each other for a long time, but that hasn’t stopped the Cleveland Cavaliers guard from giving the 2026...
articles.body:
Donovan Mitchell and Jalen Brunson have played against each other for a long time, but that hasn't stopped the Cleveland Cavaliers guard from giving the 2026 Finals MVP the praise he deserves.

The two star guards faced off, and once again it was Brunson who came out on top, as the New York Knicks secured a 121-102 win in the NBA Cup game.

Mitchell and James Harden combined for 58 points, but their efforts proved to be in vain, as the Knicks got contributions from everyone in their starting lineup, while Jose Alvarado added 21 points off the bench.

It was another disappointing defeat against the Knicks, a team that swept the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals on their way to winning an NBA championship.

Although disappointed about the result, Mitchell made sure to heap praise on how Brunson has carried the Knicks since he joined the franchise.

Donovan Mitchell speaks on Jalen Brunson's journey to helping the Knicks win a championship

Brunson and Mitchell were in the same high school class and connected over basketball. Despite the rivalry, Mitchell and Brunson share a great relationship. The Knicks guard was even at Mitchell's wedding in August.

After the game, Mitchell, who was linked with the Knicks before his move to the Cavs, was asked how he felt about Brunson achieving all the success he had with the Knicks.

He said: "Known him since high school. To see his ascension, it's always great to see someone that you know for so long, it s**** it was against us, but at the end of the day man, he is a great human. Works his b*** off and you can see that in the way he finished the season last year. To see the city rally around him, he deserves that; he's worked for it," said Mitchell during the press conference.

"My job is to go out there and to find a way to kill him every time we're out there, but you know, outside of basketball, that's a friend. Got nothing but love for him and his family. I've never seen something like that growing up. A championship here, it hurts that it was against us, but at the end of the day you've got to have nothing but respect."

Even when they met in the playoffs, Brunson heaped praise on Mitchell and his work ethic. This shows that while the NBA is all about competition, respect is at the centre of everything in the league.

articles.title: NBA Europe Arena Investment Plan Gets Wall Street Heavyweights Behind It
articles.summary: The NBA’s push into Europe just got a lot of financial muscle behind it. On Wednesday, the league announced plans to help mobilize at least €10 billion, roug...
articles.body:
The NBA's push into Europe just got a lot of financial muscle behind it. On Wednesday, the league announced plans to help mobilize at least €10 billion, roughly $11 billion, for new and renovated arenas and the entertainment districts around them across Europe. The NBA Europe arena investment initiative is meant to support the league's planned 2027 launch of a new competition with FIBA.

NBA Europe Arena Investment: Who Is Behind the €10 Billion Plan

The league is assembling a group of global investors that includes Apollo Sports Capital, Ares Management, Arctos (a KKR business), Blackstone, HPS Investment Partners, J.P. Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak , among others.

The NBA itself isn't committing to spend the full amount. Instead it's pulling together investors to help finance the projects, and it expects commitments to exceed €10 billion over time as more join. Commissioner Adam Silver called it "a major opportunity" for clubs to build facilities that honor European basketball traditions while improving the fan experience. The investors said in a joint statement they were excited to support the effort.

Projects could go beyond the buildings themselves. Depending on local needs, they could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces. The league says many major European cities lack arenas with the capacity, hospitality and media infrastructure that are standard in North American sports.

A study by The Sports Consultancy, cited by the NBA, estimates the new league could generate more than €24 billion in gross value added to Europe's GDP over its first decade, and support nearly 15,000 full-time-equivalent jobs a year. One arena has reportedly been designed with a potential London franchise in mind as its anchor.

The initiative is separate from the process of selecting team owners. Franchise cities and owners aren't finalized. Reports describe a structure with 12 permanent franchises and four rotating clubs, targeting a launch in the fall of 2027. The NBA and FIBA first confirmed the project in March 2025.

It also raises the stakes in a financial fight with the EuroLeague, which isn't backing the project . Reports say the EuroLeague committed €3.4 billion to its members over a decade, while the NBA has promised its future teams billions in revenue sharing over its first 10 years.

For now, the NBA Europe arena investment plan is a target, not a done deal. The next milestones are formal investor commitments, announced franchise cities and any settlement with the EuroLeague. But it addresses one of the biggest practical obstacles to a 2027 launch.

Christian Caple brings back the home-and-home concept for On Montlake in a discussion with Oregon writer Tyson Alger. In this case, there are certainly CFP implications because Oregon can still reach the playoff. Every game is a playoff game for the Ducks at this point, so putting a functional end to their National Championship pursuit for the 119th time would be a great feather in the cap of this UW team.

The Huskies already have a tall mountain to climb as two-TD underdogs against the resurgent Ducks. That mountain would be even more step without the best skill position players on the roster. Both Chris Lawson and Dezmen Roebuck are listed as Questionable for the Huskies on the Wednesday injury report. If either one is missing, it will make Demond Williams' job considerably tougher against a defense that is already going to create plenty of problems.

While UW Men's Basketball leaves the Maui Invitational with a 1-2 record, there were definitely bright spots in the Dawgs' performances. UW lost the 5th place game by a bucket against a solid VCU team. All three teams the Dawgs played in Hawaii were clearly superior to any of the teams on their schedule before the invitational. Even a close loss to ranked BYU and a one-possession defeat against a strong VCU team show that UW can be more competitive than wins over some of the worst teams in the NCAA.

Husky Men's Soccer will get another bite at the apple on Sunday against Big 10 Champion Indiana, this time in the third round of the NCAA tournament. Indiana beat UW just two weeks ago in a penalty shootout to take the Big 10 Tournament. They also beat the Huskies 1-0 in the regular season. articles.title: UCF vs. Boston College Men’s Basketball: Preview & Gamethread
articles.summary: Happy Turkey Day! I am thankful for (you guessed it) Luke Murray. And to add to your turkey, mashed potatoes, and whatever else will appear on your plate ton...
articles.body:
Happy Turkey Day! I am thankful for (you guessed it) Luke Murray. And to add to your turkey, mashed potatoes, and whatever else will appear on your plate tonight, we have some hoops. Boston College heads down to Florida and will face UCF today and Cincinnati tomorrow. Suffice it to say we will learn a lot about this Eagles team in the next 24 hours.

Who: Boston College Eagles (6-0) vs. UCF Knights (4-2)

Where: State Farm Field House, Kissimmee, FL

UCF enters this one having lost two in a row, albeit against Power Four competition. After taking down FGCU, Yale, South Alabama, and GA Southern, the Knights lost by three to Mississippi State and by eight to a ranked Vanderbilt squad.

For the Eagles today, the mission is simple: contain Dior Johnson. The senior guard leads the COUNTRY in points at 29 per game, along with 4.2 boards and 3.5 assists. And his production is not just the result of a high usage rate, either. He's shooting 55% from the floor and 50% from three on over four attempts per game, plus 9.7 free-throw attempts as well. My guess is we will see a heavy dose of Armoni Zeigler pestering him on the ball. Guys like Shelton or Frankel might also see some time picking him up.

Slowing Johnson down is so essential because the Knights only have one other double-digit scorer in Arturo Dean (13.8 points per game) on just 41.7% from the floor. Defensive intensity will be key for the Eagles. UCF also offers a decent matchup in terms of size; UCF only features one seven-footer in its regular rotation (John Bol).

For BC, the obvious question is whether Money Williams plays. If he does not, I'm expecting another big game from Brandon Benjamin and Zak Smrekar to pick up the slack. Ernest Shelton needs to get going. Defensively, it will be very interesting to see how well guys like Smrekar and Colby Duggan defend at the point of attack. Will a Power Four team with UCF's athleticism be able to take advantage of BC's lack of perimeter foot speed?

Should be a fun one this afternoon. Enjoy Thanksgiving, and go Eagles!

articles.body:
NBA Cup group play wraps on Friday night.

Despite being this close to the group-play finish line, there's still plenty to sort through to set the knockout-round field.

While 10 teams have been eliminated, only the undefeated Dallas Mavericks have secured their ticket to advance. And two previous unbeatens, the San Antonio Spurs and Miami Heat, just suffered their first cup losses Wednesday night.

With so much still to be decided, let's dig into what's at stake come Friday night.

Philadelphia (2-1; -12 point differential)

San Antonio (2-1; +48 point differential)

*x-clinched group; e-eliminated from knockout contention

The Magic are technically in the driver's seat for now, but they'd need both the Pistons (vs. Milwaukee) and Raptors (vs. Brooklyn) to lose Friday night to stay there. Detroit's sizable lead in point differential could be the decider here, especially with the chance to increase that against the Bucks.

All five teams have possible paths to the knockout round, but the 76ers control their destiny. Since they have the tiebreaker edge on the Heat and Cavaliers, they would advance with a road win over the Pacers on Friday.

The Celtics have the best point differential of anyone, so they're almost certainly advancing. But they still need a home win over the Hawks to clinch this group.

The Mavericks clinched this group with the Suns' loss to the Rockets on Wednesday. The Nuggets are the only other team with knockout-round hopes, but they need to a decided road win over the Jazz to have any shot at the wild card, since they're holding a negative scoring differential.

All eyes will be glued to the Gopher State on Friday, where the Timberwolves host the Grizzlies with Group B on the line. Either side takes it with a win, either pushing Minnesota's record to 4-0 or putting both clubs at 3-1 and granting Memphis the head-to-head tiebreaker.

The Kings can't advance, but the other four teams all can. The Spurs host the Lakers, and the Trail Blazers host the Warriors. Every club has a win-plus-Team-X-loss path to a Group title. The other 3-1 finisher will be scoreboard watching in hopes of landing the wild card spot.

articles.title: Ataman estalla contra la FIBA y señala a España: "Ves jugadores negros, de antiguas colonias..."
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador turco critica a la FIBA por no permitir que Tarık Biberovic juegue como nacional de pleno derecho y utiliza como ejemplo a las selecciones española y francesa
articles.summary: El seleccionador turco critica a la FIBA por no permitir que Tarık Biberovic juegue como nacional de pleno derecho y utiliza como ejemplo a las selecciones española y francesa
articles.body: Ergin Ataman ha vuelto a poner sobre la mesa el debate de las nacionalizaciones en el baloncesto internacional. En una charla con beIN Sports, el seleccionador turco criticó a la FIBA por no permitir que Tarık Biberovic obtenga la condición de jugador nacional de pleno derecho, pese a llevar diez años jugando en Turquía. En su argumentación, señaló directamente a España y Francia. "Especialmente si nos fijamos en países como España y Francia, vemos muchos jugadores negros. Todos ellos tienen jugadores que trajeron de antiguas colonias y otros países. En ese sentido, me sorprendió bastante", afirmó el técnico. Biberovic, nacido en Bosnia y Herzegovina, lleva una década compitiendo en la liga turca y cuenta con pasaporte del país. Sin embargo, la FIBA mantiene su condición de nacionalizado y no permitirá que Turquía lo incluya como jugador de origen. El presidente de la federación, Hidayet Türkoğlu, incluso visitó recientemente la sede del organismo para intentar cambiar la situación, pero recibió una respuesta negativa. "Tenía muchas esperanzas porque Tarık es turco, porque ahora es un chico turco en todos los sentidos y lo está disfrutando", lamentó Ataman. Las palabras del entrenador encontraron respuesta en Evan Fournier. El internacional francés cuestionó que se relacione el color de piel con la nacionalidad: "La última vez que estuve con Francia, en los Juegos de París, todos menos Frank Ntilikina habíamos nacido en el país; y él lo hizo en Bélgica y se mudó a Estrasburgo con tres años. ¿De qué estamos hablando? ¿Qué tiene que ver el color con la nacionalidad? ¿No eres francés si eres negro?". La negativa de la FIBA obliga a Turquía a buscar otra alternativa para ocupar la plaza de nacionalizado en el próximo Mundial. Ataman confirmó que no tomará una decisión hasta el final de la temporada. "Por ahora tenemos jugadores que pueden jugar como nacionalizados. Utilizaremos al que esté en mejor forma. Nunca se sabe, podría surgir un nombre inesperado en cualquier momento", explicó. Pese al contratiempo, el seleccionador mantiene intactas sus aspiraciones: "Con nuestro mejor equipo, por supuesto lucharemos por las medallas en el Campeonato del Mundo".

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Addresses Kevin Durant Confrontation and Ejection After Suns' Loss to Rockets
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks explained what happened on the technical foul that resulted in his ejection late in a 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks explained what happened on the technical foul that resulted in his ejection late in a 116-104 loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday.

With just seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, Brooks was assessed his second technical foul of the game when he and Rockets star Kevin Durant got in each other's faces and exchanged words:

Kevin Durant Reacts to Dillon Brooks Altercation, Making NBA History & Retirement Question in Video

Speaking to reporters after the game, Brooks suggested that the competitive juices boiled over, saying, "Just competition. It's just a battle of will. I think [Durant] started out well. So he felt like he could say a couple of things to me. It's just the competitive nature coming out. We both have it."

Just about four minutes of game time earlier, Brooks was given his first technical foul for jawing with Rockets guard Fred VanVleet, which is why the next tech resulted in an ejection.

Playing 31 minutes, Brooks finished with 12 points on 5-of-13 shooting, plus six rebounds and four assists. Meanwhile, Durant had 20 points on 7-of-15 shooting to go along with 10 rebounds and two assists in 33 minutes.

Wednesday marked a revenge game of sorts for both Brooks and Durant since Brooks is a former Rocket and Durant is a former Sun.

Fittingly, Brooks and Durant were traded for each other last year, as Brooks, Jalen Green and several other pieces were sent to Phoenix in exchange for KD.

The trade paid dividends for both teams last season, as the Rockets reached the playoffs as the No. 5 seed in the Western Conference at 52-30, while Phoenix surprisingly made the field as the No. 8 seed with a 45-37 mark.

Both the Rockets and Suns are in the playoff mix once again this season as well. With Wednesday's win, Houston improved to 14-5, putting it in a third-place tie in the Western Conference.

At 9-8, Phoenix is in 10th, but it is just 2.5 games out of the No. 6 spot, which is the cutoff before the play-in games.

Given where the Rockets and Suns are in the standings, every game between them the rest of the way will be meaningful, and it isn't outside the realm of possibility that they could meet in the playoffs.

The next Rockets vs. Suns game is scheduled for Feb. 5 when the Rockets go on the road to Phoenix.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Reacts to Dillon Brooks Altercation, Making NBA History & Retirement Question in Video
articles.summary: Kevin Durant had a busy Wednesday night in which he had an on-court altercation with Dillon Brooks and surpassed 33,000 career points to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Phoenix Suns.
articles.body:
Kevin Durant had a busy Wednesday night in which he had an on-court altercation with Dillon Brooks and surpassed 33,000 career points to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Phoenix Suns.

The situation with Brooks occurred in the fourth quarter when he and Durant started trash talking each other leading to both players receiving a technical foul.

Durant told reporters afterward what led to the altercation from his perspective while also dismissing any discussion about retirement being something he is thinking about.

"I just love basketball. That simple. We all I love to play ball. I love everything about the game, all the details that add up to winning. I care about that. I don't mind if somebody got a a grievance with me. I don't mind addressing it right there in the moment. I'm sure I said some things that he [Dillon Brooks] probably didn't like and he addressed it right there. And I can respect that as a man. And it didn't get farther than that. But if it does get farther than that, I'll be ready for that, too. "

Before the issue with Brooks happened, Durant had a memorable night when he made a three late in the second quarter to become the fifth player in NBA history with 33,000 career points.

Durant is the second-fastest player to score at least 33,000 points, reaching the milestone in just 1,220 career games. LeBron James hit the mark in his 1,216th game.

The situation between Durant and Brooks adds another chapter to their shared connection. They were traded for each other in the deal that sent Durant from Phoenix to Houston in June 2025.

Durant finished the game with 20 points and 10 rebounds to record his third double-double of the season. The Rockets (14-5) have won three of their last four games and are two games behind the Los Angeles Lakers in the loss column for the best record in the Western Conference.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball Injured, Latest on T-Wolves Star After Being Helped Off Court and HC Finch's Reaction
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball had to be helped off the court after suffering an apparent ankle injury late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 113-106 win against the Oklahoma City Thunder.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball had to be helped off the court after suffering an apparent ankle injury late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 113-106 win against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch did not have a definitive update on Ball's status after the game, but he did tell reporters , "It looked pretty bad, but I'm not sure."

Ball delivered a strong performance prior to the injury, recording 19 points on 7-of-18 shooting to go along with eight assists and seven rebounds.

Although an official statement regarding Ball's status still hasn't been made, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reported Wednesday night that Ball "was in very good spirits after the game, laughing and joking with teammates in the locker room" after the game.

Krawczynski added that Ball "seems to have avoided a major" injury.

If that is the case, it is great news for the T-Wolves, especially since superstar guard and face of the franchise Anthony Edwards is out and has been limited to only four games this season due to arthroscopic knee surgery.

With Edwards on the shelf, Ball has been the engine behind the Timberwolves' offensive attack, averaging 17.3 points per game to go along with 4.4 rebounds and a team-leading 5.7 assists and 1.6 steals.

During the offseason, Minnesota acquired Ball in a trade with the Charlotte Hornets, hoping he could be the ideal backcourt complement to Edwards.

It remains to be seen if that will be the case since Edwards has been out injured, but Ball has played a big role in keeping the T-Wolves afloat without Edwards, as they have still managed a 14-5 start, which is tied for third in the Western Conference.

Should Ball be forced to miss any time, much of the offensive burden would fall on the shoulders of Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu, who are the Timberwolves' two leading scorers among players who have appeared in at least five games this season.

McDaniels was the star for Minnesota during Wednesday's win over OKC, leading all scorers with 32 points to go along with 10 rebounds and five assists.

Bones Hyland would likely see an uptick in playing time and importance in the event of Ball missing games as well.

The Timberwolves will be back in action Friday when they host the Memphis Grizzlies.

articles.body: Welcome to a very special Thanksgiving edition of True Romance. If I'm being completely honest, I don't know how special of an edition this will be. As is often the case, this is a story of romance gone wrong. The names have been changed, but this is how the anonymous DMer remembers a messy Thanksgiving at his buddy's house a couple of years ago. With turkey and prime rib on the menu, he wrote: "I was only there for the prime rib and the free bourbon, I had no idea the Thanksgiving dinner was going to end before it ever got started." He explains his buddy Marcus was carving the turkey "like a man without a care in the world." Marcus' wife Elena was at the table, as was an overly friendly neighbor who had invited herself to Thanksgiving when her own plans "supposedly fell through." He wrote, "​Everything was fine until Marcus’s Apple Watch lit up with a notification. He had left it unmuted on the table next to his water like an idiot." His wife took a peek as the notification lit up the screen and whatever the notification said, her demeanor changed completely. "​Elena didn't scream. She didn't flip the table," he continued. "She slowly set the salt shaker down, then looked straight at Rachel." She asked, "What were you two doing last Tuesday?" Marcus froze and stopped carving the turkey. Rachel got noticeably nervous and turned red. "I still to this day don't have any idea what the notification said I haven't asked Marcus and I don't plan to," he added. "The sudden messy ending to dinner was enough." That ending to the Thanksgiving Day dinner came when Elena walked out after pouring the gravy on Marcus' lap and said, "Happy Thanksgiving, Marcus. He reached for a dinner roll and prepared for what he figured "was going to be a very long drive home." Now don’t be surprised to find out that Marcus and Elena are still married. This ruined Thanksgiving dinner that year, but not their marriage. And this is why you don’t, under any circumstances, have the neighbor you're sleeping with over for dinner. articles.title: New Draymond Green Trade Rumors on Untouchable Status in Warriors' Deadline Talks
articles.summary: Even though the Golden State Warriors have found ways to win their last two games amid Stephen Curry's absence due to injury, their trade deadline plans remain very much unsettled with Draymond Green not considered untouchable in talks.
articles.body:
Even though the Golden State Warriors have found ways to win their last two games amid Stephen Curry's absence due to injury, their trade deadline plans remain very much unsettled with Draymond Green not considered untouchable in talks.

Appearing on Sactown Sports 1140 (starts at 24:40 mark), The Athletic's Sam Amick explained Green's contract status could lead to the Warriors potentially making him available in the right scenario:

"He picked up his player option for this season, and the Warriors chose not to extend his contract at all. And even he has been pretty open about what that means. Does it mean the Warriors don't appreciate everything he's done for them over the years? No. Does it mean that he's definitely out? No. But when you have these kinds of conversations, it's the guys with the expiring contracts that are easiest to put into a deal to make the numbers work. And, you know, depending on who the other team is, it's just, you know, he's a guy that A, can still defend at a high level, still play at a high level. And B, he could help somebody as a vet on the other side, you know, and be a short-termer. So, we'll see what happens. But, but yeah, absolutely. Like, you know, they're not telling the GM on the other phone to not bring Draymond into the conversation."

Green returned to the Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million contract in the offseason. He opted out of his previous deal to give Golden State's front office more flexibility to add talent if the right opportunity presented itself, particularly during the team's pursuit of LeBron James.

After James joined the Philadelphia 76ers, Green signed a deal with the Warriors for the same money he would have received if he had opted in.

It did put Green in a position to be back on the trade market after reportedly being discussed as a potential candidate to move last season when the Warriors were looking into Giannis Antetokounmpo deals.

The Warriors looked like a surprise contender early in the season with an 8-3 record through 11 games. Curry suffered an oblique abdominal tear during a Nov. 11 game against the Houston Rockets that is expected to keep him out for at least a month.

Including the game Curry suffered the injury, the Warriors went on a five-game losing streak. They scored fewer than 100 points in each of the four games Curry didn't play at all.

The Warriors have since rebounded with back-to-back wins over the Boston Celtics and Sacramento Kings to improve to 10-8 overall. Their 129 points against the Kings were their third-most in a game all season.

If Curry returns within the expected timeframe, the Warriors will have plenty of time to make a move in the standings without thinking of dramatically altering their roster before the trade deadline in February.

The Warriors are also still planning for Jimmy Butler's return from a torn ACL at some point this season, though no official timeline has been announced yet. He is another player who could be used to help facilitate a trade with a $56.8 million expiring salary.

Green's future with the Warriors could depend on Curry's health as they evaluate their ceiling for this season. He has spent his entire 15-year career in Golden State, helping the franchise win four championships.

articles.title: España hace los deberes en Montenegro y tiene a tiro el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Oriola cambia el tono del partido con su aparición y la selección vence con autoridad para dar una zancada hacia Qatar 2027
articles.summary: Oriola cambia el tono del partido con su aparición y la selección vence con autoridad para dar una zancada hacia Qatar 2027
articles.body: La selección dio buena cuenta de Montenegro (62-93) para alcanzar la sexta victoria (su primera desde marzo) en las Ventanas de Clasificación FIBA para Qatar 2027 y tener el pase mundialista prácticamente en la mano. Con la misión de entrar entre los tres primeros del grupo I, la victoria en el vetusto Moraca de Podgorica, animoso, era imprescindible. España supo cómo ganar después de una sobresaliente segunda parte (28-52), entendió el encuentro gracias a la aparición de Oriola, los internacionales de la Euroliga respondieron bien al desafío y ahora la idea es rematar el domingo en Santiago ante Grecia, que se la juega tras su derrota en Atenas ante Georgia. Tan áspero como el clima en Podgorica (aviso rojo) y tan lluvioso que la pólvora se mojó para la selección en el inicio del partido en el vetusto Moraca. Al séptimo tiro inició su anotación España en un primer cuarto donde vivió en los umbrales de la pobreza: le podía la animosidad de Montenegro, no se encontraba en ataque, salvo Parra, y no contenía a su rival en defensa. En el minuto 7, con 12-11, en un partido donde el menú que se servía era un bocadillo de chapas, apareció Pierre Oriola para jugar el encuentro que le hemos visto cientos de veces. El disco rayado suena tan bien que es obvio contar lo siguiente: estuvo ocho minutos en cancha y le cambió la cara al partido con actitud, 10 puntos, dos triples y su pegamento en defensa. Cuando volvió al banco España pasó a dominar. Porque el ala-pívot del Manresa cambia el destino de los encuentros. También se había sumado, clarividente, Saint Supéry, (9 puntos en el segundo). El escolta del Valencia aligeró la tensión de la selección en ataque. España se había soltado con un primer demarraje, aunque Montenegro seguía a rueda (34-41, al descanso). La selección local mantuvo el espíritu tras el descanso. Pelea con el mismo candor que una cantante interpretó el himno nacional, con un sentimiento de país que sólo tiene 20 años de vida. Pero España soltó amarras. Fue incorporando jugadores a la anotación (Brizuela, Juancho, Cárdenas y Jaime Fernández) y Paulí mordía en defensa. Es un virus contagioso el de Oriol. En el minuto 27, la selección dominaba por 14 (46-60). Pese al ruidoso tambor del fondo del Moraca, Montenegro perdió su ritmo. Se desinfló. Y España se destapó con un cuarto magnífico (16-31) para resolver el encuentro (50-72 a falta del último periodo). Lo que siguió hasta el final, con la selección controlando y ampliando sus rentas, y minimizando rebeliones, fue una buena lectura: lección aprendida de la pájara de Tbilisi, cuando un colapso le costó el triunfo en Georgia después de manejar 22 puntos de ventaja. articles.title: Hannah Hidalgo Makes History Breaking Notre Dame Scoring Record, Full Stats for Elite WNBA Prospect
articles.summary: Hannah Hidalgo passed Arike Ogunbowale to become Notre Dame's all-time leading scorer in Thursday's 78-64 win over West Virginia.
articles.body:
Hannah Hidalgo passed Arike Ogunbowale to become Notre Dame's all-time leading scorer in Thursday's 78-64 win over West Virginia.

The senior guard was tied with Ogunbowale entering the contest and finished with 22 points against the Mountaineers, pushing her career total to 2,648. The record-breaking bucket came early in the first quarter:

Ogunbowale congratulated her fellow Fighting Irish star on the achievement:

Hidalgo rounded out her afternoon with six rebounds, four assists and nine steals, a performance that demonstrated why she's one of the top prospects in the 2027 WNBA draft class.

Jack Bonin projected Hidalgo to go fourth overall to the Seattle Storm in Bleacher Report's newest mock . He called her "an elite point-of-attack menace" on defense but noted she has been an inconsistent shooter across her four seasons. Her height (5'7") will also be a consideration among WNBA teams.

As a scorer, the point total speaks for itself, and Hidalgo's mark could go unchallenged for a long time.

It's difficult enough to maintain a scoring average of 24.1 points per game, which Hidalgo has done. Thanks to the transfer portal, athletes spending four seasons at one school are becoming increasingly rare as well.

Notre Dame improved its record to 7-0 with the Thanksgiving Day victory, and the next month will go a long way toward determining whether the team is a serious Final Four contender. The Fighting Irish face off with Vanderbilt, UConn, USC and South Carolina in December.

On an individual level, the difficult stretch will help to better shape Hidalgo's profile as a WNBA prospect.

articles.title: Sweeping Wahine climb back to the top as Mountain West champions
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — A new coach. A new conference. A return to the level of success for which the Hawaii women’s volleyball program is synonymous. One year after the...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — A new coach. A new conference. A return to the level of success for which the Hawaii women's volleyball program is synonymous.

One year after the worst season in Rainbow Wahine volleyball history, Hawaii, guided by the even-keeled Joshua Walker, is a conference champion again. UH swept Grand Canyon 25-16, 25-21, 25-14 in the final of the Credit Union 1 Mountain West Championship on Wednesday at Cox Pavilion.

The Rainbow Wahine (27-4), picked to finish fifth at the beginning of the season, made it look relatively easy, especially at the end, to close a dominant conference season in their first year in the Mountain West after leaving the Big West.

Hawaii didn't drop a set in two matches in the conference tournament. It lost just eight sets all season in 20 matches against conference opponents.

Four of the eight players named to the all-tournament team were from UH. Setter Adrianna Arquette and outside hitters Cha'lei Reid and Panna Ratkai were recognized along with tournament most valuable player Miliana Sylvester, who hit .647 with 12 kills in 17 swings and was in on five of Hawaii's nine blocks.

"She is just an amazing human," Walker said of Sylvester. "There is so much she has been through that has made her a stronger, higher character person. I wouldn't trade her for the world."

Hawaii had made 31 consecutive trips to the NCAA Tournament until last season, when it broke a lot of streaks.

Hawaii suffered its first losing season in program history. It did not qualify as one of six teams to make the Big West tournament after finishing no worse than second since joining the conference in 2012.

Most of the team returned and newcomers Ratkai, middle Rachel Purser and opposite Maeli Cormier were sprinkled in to provide the extra firepower UH needed on offense.

Freshman defensive specialist Cameron Holcomb joined a large group at the position that also played a big role in getting UH back to the NCAA Tournament.

"We are definitely so proud to be here. I am so excited for the girls because this was a team win," Sylvester said. "I think each and every one of us really showed up and so that makes it really, really cool to go out there and play."

Hawaii captured the 14th conference tournament championship in program history and will head to the NCAA Tournament for the 43rd time.

Any player on any night can step up and lead this team, and it was no different on Wednesday.

Ratkai, who had one kill and hit negative in Tuesday's semifinal sweep of New Mexico, led all players with 14 kills and hit .467 with two blocks and two aces.

Reid caught fire in the third set with seven of her 11 kills and hit .417. She also had a solo block that seemed to surprise her as she turned around and gave a hard clap to Walker, who was standing nearby.

"We just wanted to take care of business. Come here and work hard and do the things that we do," Reid said. "We wanted to be able to represent Hawaii well."

Grand Canyon (19-12) had won 10 of 11 matches entering the final.

Senior outside hitter Starr Williams, a transfer from Tennessee, led the Lopes with 11 kills but was held to a .103 hitting percentage.

Hawaii had six of its nine blocks in the opening set to set the tone for the match.

"She's a great player and we knew they kind of feed their outsides so if we could get more touches to slow them down, we felt we could be more successful," Sylvester said. "We felt if we could serve and get them off the net, we could make them more predictable and we did just that."

Hawaii called timeout trailing 18-16 in the second set and won nine of the final 12 points with Kahea Moriwaki helping to score five straight points from the service line.

That seemed to take the life out of the Lopes. Hawaii closed out the final set on an 8-2 run to win by double digits.

"For us, we never focus on the score. We focus on our side and the things we can do to control the match," Walker said. "We kept the pressure on them. Proud of us to finish the match off, but credit to Grand Canyon, they gave us a lot of fits and had a really great season."

Walker made the case after Tuesday's semifinal win that his team should already be in the NCAA Tournament.

Hawaii was scheduled to fly home early this morning to be home for Thanksgiving. The NCAA Selection Show is Sunday at 1 p.m.

"We just started. We're just getting going," Walker said. "I'm so glad we were able to punch our ticket the right way. We were able to play our best when our best was required and with that being said, we worked hard enough to get another opportunity. I'm so happy I keep getting to work this year."

articles.title: Goaltending leads to winning basket in UCF’s 3rd straight loss
articles.summary: It’s not often that a goaltending call ends up being the winning points in a basketball game but it happened to UCF on Thanksgiving against Boston College at...
articles.body:
It's not often that a goaltending call ends up being the winning points in a basketball game but it happened to UCF on Thanksgiving against Boston College at the ESPN Events Invitational.

After UCF's Dior Johnson tied the game at 73-73 by hitting a 3-pointer with seven seconds remaining, Boston College's Money Williams drove the length of the court to get the to basket and put up a shot off the glass. The ball was swatted away by UCF's Churchill Abass, an obvious goaltending call, putting BC up 75-73 with two seconds remaining. A desperation Johnson 3-pointer at the buzzer was no good and UCF (4-3) was sent to its third straight loss. BC stays undefeated at 7-0.

"I don't think I've ever seen that," UCF coach Johnny Dawkins said of the goaltend being the deciding points in a game. "You play long enough, you coach long enough and you're gonna see everything and that was a goaltend. He did goaltend it. I really appreciated his effort, but it was a little late."

The goaltending aside, it was defensive lapses and rebounding that spelled the difference in this game. UCF, again, struggled on the glass and was out-rebounded by nearly 20 boards by a Boston College team that wasn't necessarily considered a strong rebounding team.

"We usually hang our hat on that side of the ball and we didn't rebound well," Dawkins said. "We have to rebound the ball better and we have to make sure our guys understand the importance of not just getting a stop, but also securing the rebound.

"We held them to 39% shooting in the game, but if you're giving them second and third shot attempts you're gonna pay."

UCF had to rally from two different double-digit deficits.

The Knights were fortunate Boston College didn't run away with this one early. The Knights had just seven points in the first 10 minutes of the game, but only trailed 15-7 because BC wasn't having much luck on offense itself. Both teams had trouble finding the net, UCF hitting just 30% (10-of-33) but BC was even worse at 27% (8-of-29) in the first half.

The key for Boston College came under the net, as the Eagles took advantage of UCF's inability to rebound. A nine-rebound edge in the first half provided for several second-chance opportunities and BC built a 10-point lead in the first 14 minutes.

But the Knights finally woke up on the offensive end. Trailing 23-13, UCF went on an 11-4 run, led by Orlando native Riley Kugel's seven points to narrow the gap at halftime to 27-24.

UCF started the second half with energy. Johnson, UCF's leading scorer and the leading scorer in the country at 29 points per game, was held to just two points in the first half, but he showed determination after the break. Johnson scored six straight UCF points out of the locker room and UCF went on a 9-5 run to give the Knights their first lead of the game 33-32.

They would never lead again. BC's Williams was definitely money all day, leading all scorers with 27 points. He was fouled on a 3-pointer and made all three free throws to start an Eagles offensive barrage of 10 straight points, and UCF's momentum and energy was zapped, trailing 43-33 with 10:42 left.

The Knights kept firing away. Kugel and Carmelo Pacheco came off the bench to provide some fire and Johnson would not let the Knights whither away. UCF kept punching back, but each time the Knights got close, defensive lapses would help BC keep its distance.

Boston College got patient, working the ball around to the open man and it led to several late baskets in the shot clock.

"We gotta concentrate through the possession longer. They scored late a number of times," Dawkins said. "They are a veteran team … they've seen a lot of basketball and in situations when they had the lead, they were taking the clock down and we had to really stay focused the entire possession … that's where your lapses for rebounding become even more because you have guarded the whole possession and when the shot goes up you want to relax, but you can't. You gotta secure the ball."

Dawkins also mentioned his team's propensity to foul, and he'd also like to get that under control. The Knights sent BC to the line 35 times and the Eagles made 30.

Johnson ended up leading UCF in scoring with 23 points, while Kugel had 19 and Pacheco and Abass added 8.

The Knights are back in action again Friday in the ESPN event with a 7 p.m. matchup with Georgia

articles.title: Donovan Mitchell Addresses Jalen Brunson Rivalry, Friendship in New Video After Cavs' Loss to Knicks
articles.summary: Even though the New York Knicks have had the Cleveland Cavaliers' number lately, Donovan Mitchell has nothing but respect for Jalen Brunson amid the friendly rivalry between the two stars.
articles.body:
Even though the New York Knicks have had the Cleveland Cavaliers' number lately, Donovan Mitchell has nothing but respect for Jalen Brunson amid the friendly rivalry between the two stars.

Following the Knicks' 121-102 win over Cleveland on Wednesday, Mitchell praised Brunson's growth as a player throughout his career since they have known each other since high school while admitting it "sucks" to be on the losing end of things.

"Obviously, it sucks that it goes against us, but my boy, he's a great human," Mitchell said of Brunson. "He works his butt off, and you can see that in the way he finished the season last year, and to see the city rally around him, he deserves all that. He's worked for it."

Mitchell went on to say he is giving it his all against Brunson when they are competing on the court, but the tenor changes when they clock strikes zero:

"My job is to go out there and try to find a way to kill him every time we're out there. But outside of basketball court, as a friend that's known him for a long time, I've got nothing but love for him and his family. I've never seen something like that growing up as far as a championship here. So to see that, it hurts that it was against us, but you gotta have nothing but respect and put love for somebody who puts the time in. It's great to see that."

Brunson was held to 19 points on 6-of-22 shooting in the win, but Jose Alvarado sparked the Knicks with 21 points off the bench.

Mitchell did his part to help the Cavs with a game-high 30 points. It was his fifth 30-point game of the season, but Cleveland is just 1-4 when he hits that mark.

Before being traded to Cleveland by the Utah Jazz, Mitchell was heavily linked to the Knicks so much that New York officials were reportedly "shocked and disappointed" he didn't end up with them after the 2022 deal went down.

That was the same offseason the Knicks signed Brunson to a four-year, $104 million contract in free agency. It's safe to say things have worked out just fine for them since that deal.

Since the start of the 2025-26 season, the Cavaliers have lost eight of 10 games to the Knicks. The record includes New York's four-game sweep in the Eastern Conference Finals.

During this 10-game run, five of New York's wins have been by at least 10 points.

Mitchell has at least been doing all he can to help Cleveland get over the hump. He has scored at least 30 points five times against the Knicks since the start of last season.

Wednesday's loss dropped the Cavs' record to 9-10 overall. It's the latest into a season they have been under .500 since the 2021-22 season when they also started 9-10 en route to a 44-38 finish.

articles.title: 5 Takeaways from Michigan’s loss to Miami
articles.summary: The Hurricanes dominated the game, cruising to victory as Michigan lost in blowout fashion for the second game in a row:
articles.body:
You may have missed it while your family was eating Thanksgiving dinner, but the Michigan Wolverines lost handily to the No. 17 Miami Hurricanes, 97-70.

Coming off of a demoralizing loss to Creighton , Michigan needed to bounce back against Miami (ranked 29th in KenPom) to avoid a three-game skid. Miami was picked to finish fourth in the ACC , and the Hurricanes are tough to score on in the interior, ranking fourth in the country in opponent's two-point percentage (38.5) and fourth in opponent's offensive rebounding percentage (22.7). Forward Shelton Henderson leads Miami in scoring (14.3 points per game), and the Hurricanes have several notable transfers, including Acaden Lewis (Villanova), Malik Reneau (Indiana) and L.J. Cason (Michigan), who is recovering from a torn ACL.

Miami was the better team in the first half, making nearly 60 percent of their shots and controlling the pace of the game. The Hurricanes re-asserted dominance at the start of the second half, jumping out to a 15-point lead that ballooned into a 25-point lead in a hurry.

This was a weird environment for a game, with the two teams playing in the middle of Thanksgiving Day in a gym that was mayyyybe 20 percent full based on how it looked on TV. So it's a bad setting to mount a comeback, but that's not an excuse; this was the second game in a row that the Wolverines straight up gave up.

This is now Michigan's first three-game losing streak since March 2-9 in 2025 in Dusty May's first year. This is a group that is now 3-4, and has played uninspiring basketball on both sides of the floor. Something has to change with the energy on this team, especially on defense; if not, this season could get UGLY.

And to add injury to insult, fifth-year wing Roddy Gayle Jr. left the game after rolling his ankle. So a Michigan team that was already struggling with depth may be without one of it's best shot creators for a little while.

Here are some takeaways from another loss. Happy Thanksgiving, I guess.

Miami went on a 10-2 run at the start of the second half to put Michigan in a deep hole, as the Wolverines missed it's first three shots of the half and turned the ball over three times before the first media timeout of the second half.

Miami outscored Michigan, 42-18, before the final TV timeout of the second half, and by then, the game was well out of hand.

The Wolverines ran out of steam offensively as effort wained in the second half. This was ugly basketball that we haven't seen since the end of Juwan Howard era; something's got to change.

The Tennessee transfer was rock solid on the interior in this one, surpassing his season average for points per game (16.4) with 17 points late in the first half. Per the ESPN broadcast crew, that was the second-most points he's scored in a half in his four-year career.

Like we saw with Vlad Goldin two years ago, Estrella absorbed contact in the paint with ease, scoring on hook shots and making his bunnies to stay efficient around the rim.

Estrella finished the game with 21 points and was one of the few bright spots in an otherwise dreadful offensive performance by the Wolverines.

Coming off of a rough performance on Tuesday, Cadeau did a great job directing the offense early in this one; per the ESPN broadcast, he either scored or assisted on 25 of Michigan's first 27 points over the first 13 minutes of the game.

Cadeau did a great job steadily creating buckets for the Wolverines, recording seven assists in the first half and eight assists in the whole game. Estrella was the beneficiary of the dump down passes from Cadeau and other drivers, a large portion of which came off of well-placed touch passes.

Cadeau did fantastic in the first half, but struggled in the second half, going 1/9 from the field.

Michigan's good start quickly gets erased with sharpshooting by Miami

After getting out to shaky starts all season, the Wolverines had an eight-point lead in the first eight minutes of the game. Elliot Cadeau and J.P. Estrella each had seven points early, as the Wolverines went on a 7-0 run and played with energy after a lackluster effort on Tuesday.

The Michigan offense went cold, though, as Miami hit seven shots in a row as part of a 17-3 lead to take a 30-24 lead late in the first half. Like we saw in the Creighton loss, Miami got open looks and kept knocking them down, as Michigan was a touch late on defensive rotations.

Miami ended it's superb first half on a 7-0 run to go into halftime with a seven-point lead, as the Hurricanes knocked down 59 percent of it's shots in the first 20 minutes.

Not a great showing by Michigan's defense

Michigan has not looked much like the defensive juggernaut that it was last season.

Miami got a lot of open shots early in this one and knocked them down, with the Hurricanes making 16 of it's first 28 shots and five of it's first 10 threes.

Defense is always hard to assess on an initial watch, but on that initial watch, I thought Michigan looked slow on rotations and didn't play great on-ball defense early, allowing Miami to drive to the rim with relative ease. Shelton Henderson played a great game, drawing fouls and driving past Michigan defenders on his way to 25 points.

Defense was this team's calling card throughout the National Championship run, and Mike Boynton Jr. still has a hand in the defense as serving as the unit's coordinator the past seasons. Aside from rim protection, Michigan has been underwhelming on defense and has to improve on that end of the floor as the year goes along.

Michigan finishes out the consolation bracket tomorrow, with the seventh-place Black Friday game tipping off at 5:30 p.m. EST. The Wolverines will face either No. 15 Alabama (22nd in KenPom entering today) or Kansas State (112nd).

With Michigan not being the championship of the Players Era 16, they will play Mississippi Valley State on Tuesday, Dec. 1. That game back at the Crisler Center tips off at 7 p.m. EST.

articles.title: Michigan mashed by Miami in another blowout loss at Players Era 16
articles.summary: In its second game at the Vegas tournament, Michigan was feasted on by Miami and turned in another uninspiring performance in a 97-70 rout.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — The Wolverines were on the hunt for a Thanksgiving treat. But as it turns out, they were on the menu.

In its second game at the Players Era 16, Michigan was feasted on by No. 17 Miami (Fla.) and turned in another uninspiring performance in a 97-70 rout at T-Mobile Arena on Thursday, Nov. 26.

J.P. Estrella had 21 points, Trey McKenney scored 16 and Elliot Cadeau had 15 points and eight assists for Michigan (3-4), which has lost three straight and is off to its worst start since 2007-08.

The Wolverines have one more shot to salvage their trip and leave the Vegas tournament with a win. They will face the No. 15 Alabama-Kansas State loser in their third and final game at 5:30 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 27.

Against Miami (6-2), it was a similar script like Michigan's other losses this season. The Wolverines were competitive for the first 10 minutes or so until the contest slowly started to spiral and they fell behind by a deficit that's too much to overcome.

Following a first half where Michigan's defense did little to slow down Miami, not much changed after the break. The Hurricanes opened the second half with an uncontested dunk that kicked off a 22-4 burst and the Wolverines fell behind, 74-49, with 12:56 to play.

During Miami's big run, Moustapha Thiam — limited to five minutes in the first half due to foul trouble — and Cadeau both picked up their fourth foul three minutes into the second half. Michigan missed eight of its first nine shots out of the break. To add salt in the wound, Miami capped its run with a 3-pointer following a turnover from Roddy Gayle Jr., who exited favoring his left leg after stepping on an opponent's foot during a drive to the rim.

The Wolverines trailed by at least 21 points and by as much as 31 points over the final 11 minutes, as they were handed a second straight blowout loss. Michigan lost to Creighton, 99-73, in the opening round on Nov. 24.

Michigan shot 36.9% from the field for the game, a miserable 23.1% in a 25-point second half and 7-for-29 from 3-point range.

Shelton Henderson had 25 points and 10 rebounds and Dante Allen scored 21 to lead Miami. The Hurricanes shot 59.4% from the field in the first half and 56.3% for the game.

Miami entered the game shooting 29% from deep and averaging seven 3-pointers per game. It made seven deep balls in the first half and finished 9-for-21 from beyond the arc.

Both teams were down a player. The Hurricanes were without starter Caleb Gaskins, who ranked second on the team in scoring (11.4 points) and rebounding (5.9). The Wolverines were down reserve Oscar Goodman, who was held out with a medical issue.

After a pair of rough outings the past two games, Cadeau got off to a tremendous start and had a hand in Michigan's first 21 points. He scored in the paint and from beyond the arc. He connected with Moustapha Thiam on an alley-oop. He found Estrella for a corner 3, for a layup on an inbounds pass and for another bucket down low.

During one sequence, Cadeau grabbed a defensive rebound, took it the other way and knocked down a pull-up jumper. Then after another stop on defense, Cadeau pushed the ball and nearly lost it in traffic, but he managed to bat the ball out to Trey McKenney for a 3-pointer. That capped a 7-0 spurt, gave Michigan a 21-13 lead with 12:32 left in the first half and forced a Miami timeout.

But like the past two games, the opponent responded with a run to wipe away the good vibes. This time, the Hurricanes rattled off a 16-3 burst and made seven consecutive shots to pull in front 29-24, with Michigan's lone bucket during the run coming on a driving layup by Cadeau.

Miami stayed in front as Michigan had no answers on defense and foul trouble became problematic. Cadeau picked up his second foul at the 7:12 mark. Thiam picked up his third foul at the 6:22 mark. McKenney fouled Allen on a 3-pointer for a four-point play. The Wolverines went down by as much as nine and entered the break trailing 52-45.

articles.title: The Timberwolves Have One Game to Do Something They’ve Never Done
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have already shown they can keep the season alive without Anthony Edwards. On Friday, they’ll have a […]
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have already shown they can keep the season alive without Anthony Edwards . On Friday, they'll have a chance to take that success somewhere the franchise has never been before.

Minnesota hosts the Memphis Grizzlies with the NBA Cup's West Group B on the line. Both teams won Wednesday, and the winner of Friday's matchup will claim the group and advance to the tournament's knockout stage.

For the Timberwolves, that would mean reaching the NBA Cup quarterfinals for the first time since the competition began. It would also give a team off to a 14-5 start another meaningful early-season test.

The Wolves earned the opportunity with a 113-106 road win over Oklahoma City on Wednesday. Jaden McDaniels scored 32 points, grabbed 10 rebounds and handed out five assists as Minnesota improved to 3-0 in group play. The victory came with a concern, though: LaMelo Ball left late in the fourth quarter after injuring his left ankle.

Coach Chris Finch did not have a diagnosis immediately after the game. Ball was in good spirits in the locker room, according to Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic , but his availability for Friday remained uncertain.

The Wolves and Grizzlies don't need to wait for another result to find out whether they've won their group. After Memphis also won Wednesday, Friday's winner will take West Group B.

Minnesota has already seen what this version of the Grizzlies can do. The teams met at Target Center on Saturday, when the Wolves turned a slow start into a 104-95 victory. Memphis scored 34 points in the first quarter, but Minnesota held the Grizzlies to a combined 28 in the second and third quarters to take control.

Friday brings a different set of stakes. A regular-season win would help either team in the Western Conference standings, while the group title would put the winner one step closer to competing for the NBA Cup.

The players also have another reason to pay attention. When McDaniels was asked after the Oklahoma City game about the chance to advance, he pointed to the reward waiting further down the road.

"Just another step closer to the money," McDaniels said .

Dosunmu acknowledged the financial incentive, too. But he also emphasized what the opportunity means for a group trying to build something together.

"You want to win, you want to advance, you want to have a chance," Dosunmu said . "So it gives more of an incentive to go out there and compete."

Minnesota's path to this point hasn't been straightforward. Edwards has been out since undergoing knee surgery after the opening week of the season, while Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark have also been sidelined.

The Wolves have continued to find contributors. Terrence Shannon Jr. scored a career-high 34 points in the first of two wins over Portland. Dosunmu followed with 30 in the second. McDaniels has taken his offensive game to another level, scoring at least 30 in consecutive wins over Brooklyn and Oklahoma City.

That depth mattered again Wednesday when Ball left with the game still close. Dosunmu assumed more of the ball-handling responsibility and made timely shots as Minnesota finished the win.

Whether the Wolves will need to do the same against Memphis remains to be seen. Ball had 19 points and eight assists against the Thunder before his injury, and his playmaking would be difficult to replace if he's unavailable.

Even with the uncertainty, Minnesota has put itself in the position it wanted: one game, at home, with the group title available.

The Wolves have bigger goals than an NBA Cup appearance. But Friday offers a chance to play a meaningful game in November, reward their early-season work and take the franchise somewhere it hasn't been in the competition.

As McDaniels put it after the win in Oklahoma City, Minnesota is another step closer. Now the Wolves have to take the next one.

articles.title: Michigan basketball gets hammered in Las Vegas as Miami cruises
articles.summary: The Wolverines had three blowouts in Las Vegas in 2025. This time around, Michigan has been on the wrong end of a pair of demolitions.
articles.body:
Michigan basketball 's skid has continued an blowout fashion.

The Wolverines have now lost three consecutive games after falling 97-70 to Miami on Thursday, Nov. 26, in the Players Era Championship tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Mike Boynton's team gave up more than 50 points in the opening half for the second time in as many games, fell behind by 10 early in the second half and didn't get closer than that the rest of the way.

U-M (3-4) once again got lit up from long range, as Jai Lucas' group went 9 of 21 on 3s. It didn't help that moments after halftime, Elliot Cadeau committed his third foul 90 feet from the hoop while Moustapha Thiam committed his fourth just more than two minutes into the second half.

Miami (6-2), which led by seven at the break, opened the second half on 22-4 run and never looked back. Matters got worse when Roddy Gayle jr. rolled his ankle just less than seven minutes into the half and had to be helped off the court by trainers.

J.P. Estrella continues to be U-M's most consistent player, scoring a team-high 21 points. Cadeau and Trey McKenney were both relatively quiet, scoring 15 and 16 points, respectively. But it was the defense that was the main problem, as the Hurricanes shot 56% from the field.

Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia .

articles.title: 76ers rule out Jaylen Brown (hamstring), list Joel Embiid (illness) as questionable for Friday's game vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Brown may have re-injured the hamstring that caused him to miss two games last week, and Embiid could miss his third consecutive game.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night.

Shooting guard Jaylen Brown has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games.

Brown picked up the hamstring issue in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return. The guard missed two games last week with a left hamstring strain, but returned to action against the Portland Trail Blazers and played 29 minutes.

Toward the end of the first half, the Philadelphia guard reached toward his left hamstring and shook his head before checking himself out of the game.

Embiid is dealing with an illness, though not much has been released about what symptoms he may be dealing with. Regardless, he has missed two consecutive games. The center was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat, but was downgraded before the game.

With no Embiid and no Brown for a half, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey took over and led the 76ers to a win over the Heat on Wednesday. James logged his first triple-double as a 76er with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Maxey added 30 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists.

The win moved Philadelphia to 15-4. Friday's game against Indiana is the front end of a back-to-back, and a win would help the 76ers clinch their NBA Cup Group.

articles.title: Henderson, Allen power No. 17 Miami to a 97-70 win over Michigan at Players Era 16 tournament
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Shelton Henderson had 25 points, 10 rebounds and six assists as No. 17 Miami cruised past Michigan 97-70 in a consolation-round game of the...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Shelton Henderson had 25 points, 10 rebounds and six assists as No. 17 Miami cruised past Michigan 97-70 in a consolation-round game of the Players Era 16 tournament on Thursday.

Dante Allen scored 21 points for the Hurricanes (6-2), while Nick Dorn added 14, Aceden Lewis 12 and Malik Reneau 11.

J.P. Estrella led Michigan (3-4) with 21 points. Trey McKenney added 16 points and Elliot Cadeau 15.

Miami opened the second half with a 12-2 run to take a 64-47 lead with 15:29 remaining. Henderson scored six points during the outburst. Miami's largest lead was 31 points, while Michigan got no closer than nine in the second half.

The Hurricanes shot 56.3% (36 of 65) from the field, including 42.9% (9 of 21) from 3-point range.

Miami's largest lead of the first half was 52-43 with 53 seconds remaining. The advantage came during a seven-point run, sparked by 3-pointers from Reneau and Allen, along with a free throw by Allen.

The Hurricanes took a 52-45 lead into halftime. Henderson had 17 first-half points for Miami. Estrella led Michigan with 17.

Michigan held an eight-point lead, 21-13, with 12:32 remaining after a seven-point run capped by a 3-pointer from McKenney. Miami responded with a nine-point run to take a 22-21 lead with 10:26 left in the half.

Miami: Will play the winner of No. 15 Alabama-Kansas State for fifth place on Friday.

Michigan: Will play the loser of No. 15 Alabama-Kansas State for seventh place on Friday.
